results.title: I Tried Using Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots to Save on Groceries. They're Not Quite There Yet - CNET
results.description: I tried using AI agents to build me the cheapest grocery order possible. They exhibited a startling lack of curiosity and autonomous thinking.
extra_snippets: The first step in finding cheaper groceries with AI agents is to check which sites and stores they can access for price comparisons. Where both agents missed a step was in the limitations they put on their searches, at first only looking at the retailers I had shown via my receipts and a few other big-name grocery stores. I clarified in the chats and in a 20-minute voice conversation with Muse and a 14-minute voice conversation with Dots that they should expand their horizons and look at discount online retailers like Martie.com, and check what they could around advertised pricing and offerings at local farmers’ markets.

Neither of the tools checked Trader Joe’s. Muse said that the grocery chain doesn’t show prices of its products online, despite me finding that the Trader Joe’s website shows prices of its products online. Both Dots and Muse admitted to only checking the local store’s pages when asked. You could spend some time making a list from scratch of all the groceries you might need every two weeks and give that list to the AI agent for its search.

I had some receipts saved, and the AI agents I used for this test were able to put together an accurate grocery list from them. I also provided emails showing receipts from online orders of household items and groceries for the past month to build my orders. Muse took my receipts and concluded that, surprise, surprise, shopping at Gelson’s was not as cost-effective as shopping at Walmart.

I was keen to see how the always-on AI agents would handle managing the recurring needs of a small household and if they might make any autonomous suggestions meant to save me money in ways I hadn’t anticipated. At no point did Muse seem to be actually thinking outside the strict parameters of the review of the items on the receipts I sent.
